summary.headline: ABLBL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore and EBITDA 14% to Rs 327 crore, with margin up 50 bps to 16%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore, the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with EBITDA up 14% to Rs 327 crore and PAT up 21% to Rs 29 crore. Lifestyle Brands grew 10% to Rs 1,725 crore at an 18.5% EBITDA margin, while Emerging Brands grew 19% to Rs 332 crore at a 4.3% margin. Management attributed a modest demand moderation to adhik maas during the peak wedding period and a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2 that depressed wholesale growth to 5%. Gross margin contracted about 150 bps, which management attributed to channel mix and provisioning rather than raw material costs.

financial_highlights.change: Down ~150 bps YoY per analyst question; management called it marginally lower

segments.name: Lifestyle Brands
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,725 crore (+10% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 319 crore at 18.5% margin. Retail grew 10% with 7% LFL across almost 3,000 stores; e-commerce grew 23% group-wide and over 50% on the company's own platform.

segments.name: Emerging Brands (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 332 crore (+19% YoY), with retail LFL of 11% and e-commerce growth above 30%. Retail network crossed 400 stores; EBITDA margin 4.3%, up 240 bps.

segments.name: Channels (group)
segments.commentary: Retail grew 10% with 8% LFL, the seventh straight quarter of LFL growth. Wholesale grew 5% on primary billing, though underlying secondary growth was early double-digit.

guidance_outlook: Gross store additions of more than 300 in FY27, with net additions of 150-200 after closures of about 120-140 stores.
Cost inflation of 3-4% expected for Q2-Q3 FY27 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages; mostly to be offset by productivity and cost rationalisation, plus small price hikes.
Management expects Q1+Q2 wholesale primary billing to even out, with the Q1 shortfall moving into Q2.
Small-town retail (about 500 stores) is about 15-16% of retail revenue and is expected to exceed 20% of portfolio over the next three to four years.
Management aims for sustained double-digit growth and margin expansion; it expects retail to grow in early double digits.
Reebok revenue is about Rs 500 crore (from about Rs 250 crore at acquisition); management sees close to 20% long-term growth possible.
capex_capacity: Retail footprint of 3,362 stores (about 5 million sq ft) across more than 800 cities and towns at quarter end; more than 65 gross openings in Q1 (Aditya Bansal's question: 68 gross).
Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha; Karnataka concentration is limited.
Reebok has about 200 stores versus 500-700 for other premium brands, indicating a long retail runway.
Van Heusen Innerwear distribution is about 38,000-40,000 outlets; management expects roughly 20% network addition over the next couple of years.
Two Reebok factories still operate outside India pending BIS annual renewal; domestic sourcing is being built up.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand was broadly consistent with the prior-year trend; adhik maas caused modest moderation in the peak wedding period.
Wholesale grew 5%, with a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2; management says secondary was early double-digit.
Small-town stores grew over 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros; small-town growth has been double-digit for five consecutive quarters.
Price hikes were small and varied by brand and category, taken to offset input-cost increases; management says no meaningful apparel inflation is visible.
Marketing spend was about 3.5% of sales in Q1, down from last year because of IPL spend in the base quarter.
E-commerce profitability is said to be close to retail profitability, with growth now coming without deep discounting.
Quick commerce is small for the company; innerwear is the largest category there.
Casual wear share is rising by 2-3 percentage points a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why the divergence between primary and secondary sales in Lifestyle wholesale, and how will it evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: A 10-15 day festive timing shift moved primary billing into Q2; management expects Q1 and Q2 combined to be as strong as other channels.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation is expected and will prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 saw marginal to no cost pressure. Management expects 3-4% cost increase in Q2-Q3 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages, offset mainly by productivity and some price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 150 bps gross margin contraction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited channel mix and slightly higher inventory-age provisioning, not raw material costs, and said the effect is not material and will even out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to Karnataka minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Garmenting was never part of the notified hike, which is under High Court challenge. Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

qa_highlights.question: How are the net store adds and LFL growth reconciled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to more than 300 gross and 150-200 net additions in FY27 after 120-140 closures; network growth of 5-6% plus 7-8% LFL supports early double-digit retail growth.

qa_highlights.question: How do small-town and Tier 1 growth compare, and how is Gen-Z targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Tier 3-4 is growing above 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros. Gen-Z is served through sub-brands and collections (for example Peter England's Vybe), with no share figures disclosed.

risks_watch: Wholesale growth of 5% and gross margin contraction of about 150 bps in Q1; watch whether the festive shift reverses in Q2.
3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3 and the wage-regulation outcome in Karnataka at the High Court.
Consumer wallet pressure from inflation; management says it has seen no meaningful demand shift so far but is cautious about H2.
Reebok BIS certification risk on imports from factories outside India, renewed annually.
Net store additions of 150-200 against a gross plan above 300; watch LFL sustainability through closures.
key_quotes: So, when you look at Quarter 2, you will find the Quarter 1 plus Quarter 2 in as strong a place as rest of the channels.
We expect a major part of it comes through productivity and the rest through cost rationalization.
But we are cautious that this may play out in the second half of the year.
Over the years, we have managed to bring this channel profitability very close to our retail profitability.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on headline growth, margin expansion and store roll-out, and openly described Q1 wholesale as a timing shift. It was cautious on H2 demand from consumer wallet inflation and on 3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3, and it deflected on brand-wise revenue splits and gross margin drivers.

Van Heusen Innerwear distribution network addition of roughly 20% (from 38,000-40,000 outlets) over next couple of years

growth.why: Management guides more than 300 gross and 150-200 net store additions in FY27 and expects retail in early double digits, backed by store rollout and small-town growth; no explicit revenue growth % was guided, and the brief gives no order book or capex figures, so backing is partial.
